Conversational and almost always critical; the speaker is often close to the topic (family, colleagues, things they own). Compare といえば (N3), which is neutral.

26.title: 〜に言わせれば
26.structure: Noun (person) + に言わせれば・に言わせると
26.explanation: Presents a particular person's opinion, often a strong or different one.

examples.jp: 父に言わせれば、最近の若者は努力が足りないそうだ。
examples.en: According to my father, young people today don't try hard enough.

examples.jp: 私に言わせれば、その計画は無理がある。
examples.en: If you ask me, that plan is unrealistic.

26.summary: に言わせれば introduces someone's own, often critical, opinion — 'if you ask X'.
26.details:
父**に言わせれば**、最近の若者は努力が足りないそうだ。
*(According to my father, young people today don't try hard enough.)*
私**に言わせれば**、その計画は無理がある。
*(If you ask me, that plan is unrealistic.)*

With 私, it emphasizes the speaker's own frank opinion. The causative 言わせる ('let say') gives the sense 'if X were allowed to speak'. The opinion often differs from the general view.

26.title: 〜きっての
26.meaning: The best in ~ / The most ~ in ~
26.structure: Noun (group, place) + きっての + Noun
26.explanation: Someone or something is the best or most outstanding in a group or place.

examples.jp: 彼は社内きっての切れ者だ。
examples.en: He's the sharpest person in the company.

examples.jp: ここは町きっての名店として知られている。
examples.en: This place is known as the best restaurant in town.

26.summary: きっての means 'the best/most outstanding in X'.
26.details:
彼は社内**きっての**切れ者だ。
*(He's the sharpest person in the company.)*
ここは町**きっての**名店として知られている。
*(This place is known as the best restaurant in town.)*

The noun is a group or area (社内, 学内, 日本, 当代 'of the present age'). It's always used as praise. 切っての in kanji.

26.title: 〜ながらに／〜ながらの
26.structure: Noun / Verb (ます-stem) + ながらに・ながらの
26.explanation: A state continues unchanged, in a few set expressions.

examples.jp: この町には昔ながらの家並みが残っている。
examples.en: This town still has rows of houses just as they used to be.

examples.jp: 彼女は涙ながらに事故の様子を語った。
examples.en: She described the accident in tears.

26.summary: ながらに／ながらの describe a state that stays the same — in set phrases like 昔ながら.
26.details:
この町には昔**ながらの**家並みが残っている。
*(This town still has rows of houses just as they used to be.)*
彼女は涙**ながらに**事故の様子を語った。
*(She described the accident in tears.)*

Used in fixed expressions: 昔ながらの ('traditional'), 生まれながらに ('from birth'), 涙ながらに ('in tears'), いながらにして ('without leaving home'). Not productive with other words, and different from ながら ('while') and ながらも ('although').

27.title: 〜から〜に至るまで
27.structure: Noun 1 + から + Noun 2 + に至るまで (にいたるまで)
27.explanation: By citing items at either extreme of a group, it indicates that something applies to absolutely everything in that group.

examples.jp: 自転車のねじから人工衛星の部品に至るまで、どれもこの工場で作っています。
examples.en: We make everything in this factory from bicycle screws to satellite components.

examples.jp: クラシックからJ-popに至るまで、当店ではどんなジャンルの音楽でもご用意しております。
examples.en: We offer all kinds of music in this shop, from classical to J-pop.

27.summary: から〜に至るまで cites two extreme ends of a group to emphasize that something applies to absolutely everything within it — 'from A all the way to Z.'
27.details:
自転車のねじから人工衛星の部品**に至るまで**、どれもこの工場で作っています。
*(We make everything in this factory, from bicycle screws all the way to satellite components.)*
クラシックからJ-pop**に至るまで**、当店ではどんなジャンルの音楽でもご用意しております。
*(We offer every genre of music in this shop, from classical all the way to J-pop.)*

The two items cited (自転車のねじ ↔ 人工衛星の部品; クラシック ↔ J-pop) are chosen specifically because they're at opposite extremes — the whole point is that if even these two very different things are covered, everything in between must be too.

27.title: 〜に至る／〜に至って（は）
27.meaning: Reach ~ / Only when it came to ~ / As for ~
27.structure: Noun / Verb (Dictionary) + に至る・に至って・に至っては
27.explanation: Reaching an extreme point. に至って: only when things reached that point. に至っては: as for X (the most extreme example).

examples.jp: 事故が起きるに至って、ようやく対策がとられた。
examples.en: Measures were only taken once an accident had happened.

examples.jp: 家族全員が反対している。妹に至っては、口もきいてくれない。
examples.en: My whole family is against it. As for my sister, she won't even speak to me.

27.summary: に至る means reaching an extreme point; に至って: 'only when it came to X'; に至っては: 'and as for X (the extreme case)'.
27.details:
事故が起きる**に至って**、ようやく対策がとられた。
*(Measures were only taken once an accident had happened.)*
家族全員が反対している。妹**に至っては**、口もきいてくれない。
*(My whole family is against it. As for my sister, she won't even speak to me.)*

に至る alone means 'to lead to' (死に至る病気, 'a fatal disease'). に至って is often followed by ようやく／やっと, criticizing a late response. に至っては picks out the most extreme item in a list. See also から〜に至るまで (this lesson).

27.title: 〜ぐるみ
27.meaning: Including all of ~ / The whole ~ together
27.explanation: Something involves an entire group, all together.

examples.jp: 私たちは家族ぐるみで付き合っている。
examples.en: Our families are friends with each other.

examples.jp: 地域ぐるみで子どもの安全を守る活動をしている。
examples.en: The whole community works together to keep children safe.

27.summary: ぐるみ means 'the whole X together' — involving everyone in the group.
27.details:
私たちは家族**ぐるみ**で付き合っている。
*(Our families are friends with each other.)*
地域**ぐるみ**で子どもの安全を守る活動をしている。
*(The whole community works together to keep children safe.)*

Used with a limited set of nouns: 家族, 町, 地域, 会社, 組織. 組織ぐるみの犯罪 means 'an organization-wide crime'. It comes from くるむ ('to wrap').

27.title: 〜なりに／〜なりの
27.meaning: In one's own way ~ / As far as ~ allows
27.structure: Noun / Verb・Adj (Plain) + なりに・なりの + Noun
27.explanation: Within someone's own limits or position, they do the best they can.

examples.jp: 子どもは子どもなりに、親のことを心配している。
examples.en: Children worry about their parents in their own way.

examples.jp: 私なりの方法で問題を解決してみます。
examples.en: I'll try to solve the problem in my own way.

27.summary: なりに means 'in one's own way, within one's limits'.
27.details:
子どもは子ども**なりに**、親のことを心配している。
*(Children worry about their parents in their own way.)*
私**なりの**方法で問題を解決してみます。
*(I'll try to solve the problem in my own way.)*

Often acknowledges effort despite limits: 子どもなりに, 若いなりに. With 私, it's modest: 私なりに頑張りました. それなりに means 'to a reasonable extent'. Different from なり ('as soon as', Lesson 4).

28.title: 〜をよそに
28.explanation: Someone acts while ignoring others' worries, expectations or surroundings.

examples.jp: 親の心配をよそに、彼は一人で海外へ旅立った。
examples.en: Ignoring his parents' worries, he set off abroad alone.

examples.jp: 住民の反対をよそに、工事は進められた。
examples.en: The construction went ahead despite residents' opposition.

28.summary: をよそに means acting while ignoring others' concerns or opposition.
28.details:
親の心配**をよそに**、彼は一人で海外へ旅立った。
*(Ignoring his parents' worries, he set off abroad alone.)*
住民の反対**をよそに**、工事は進められた。
*(The construction went ahead despite residents' opposition.)*

The noun is usually others' feelings or reactions: 心配, 期待, 反対, 不安. よそ means 'elsewhere', so the image is pushing those concerns aside. It describes other people's actions.

28.title: 〜をものともせず（に）
28.structure: Noun + をものともせず（に）
28.explanation: Overcoming a hardship or danger bravely, without being discouraged.

examples.jp: 彼女は足のけがをものともせず、最後まで走り抜いた。
examples.en: Undaunted by her leg injury, she ran all the way to the end.

examples.jp: 救助隊は激しい雨をものともせずに、捜索を続けた。
examples.en: Braving the heavy rain, the rescue team continued the search.

28.summary: をものともせず describes bravely overcoming a hardship — 'undaunted by X'.
28.details:
彼女は足のけが**をものともせず**、最後まで走り抜いた。
*(Undaunted by her leg injury, she ran all the way to the end.)*
救助隊は激しい雨**をものともせずに**、捜索を続けた。
*(Braving the heavy rain, the rescue team continued the search.)*

The noun is an obstacle (けが, 危険, 困難, 反対, 嵐). It expresses admiration and describes others, not the speaker. Compare をよそに, which means ignoring others' concerns, not overcoming danger.

28.title: 〜をいいことに
28.structure: Noun / Verb (Plain) + の + をいいことに
28.explanation: Someone exploits a situation to do something they shouldn't.

examples.jp: 親が留守なのをいいことに、彼は友達を家に呼んで騒いだ。
examples.en: Taking advantage of his parents being away, he invited friends over and partied.

examples.jp: 先生が何も言わないのをいいことに、生徒たちは宿題をしなくなった。
examples.en: Taking advantage of the teacher saying nothing, the students stopped doing homework.

28.summary: をいいことに means exploiting a situation to do something one shouldn't.
28.details:
親が留守なの**をいいことに**、彼は友達を家に呼んで騒いだ。
*(Taking advantage of his parents being away, he invited friends over and partied.)*
先生が何も言わないの**をいいことに**、生徒たちは宿題をしなくなった。
*(Taking advantage of the teacher saying nothing, the students stopped doing homework.)*

Always critical. The situation is often an absence of control (留守, 黙っている, 優しい). It describes other people's behavior.

28.title: 〜にかこつけて
28.meaning: Using ~ as an excuse / Under the pretext of ~
28.explanation: Using something as a pretext to do what one actually wants to do.

examples.jp: 出張にかこつけて、観光を楽しんだ。
examples.en: Using the business trip as an excuse, I enjoyed some sightseeing.

examples.jp: 彼は病気にかこつけて、面倒な仕事を断った。
examples.en: He used illness as an excuse to turn down a troublesome job.

28.summary: にかこつけて means using X as a pretext for doing something else.
28.details:
出張**にかこつけて**、観光を楽しんだ。
*(Using the business trip as an excuse, I enjoyed some sightseeing.)*
彼は病気**にかこつけて**、面倒な仕事を断った。
*(He used illness as an excuse to turn down a troublesome job.)*

The noun is the excuse (仕事, 病気, 用事, 雨) and the second clause is the real purpose. The tone is often critical or self-mocking. かこつける means 'to make a pretext of'.

29.title: 〜にかまけて
29.meaning: Being too wrapped up in ~ (to do other things)
29.explanation: Being so absorbed in one thing that one neglects something else.

examples.jp: 仕事にかまけて、家族との時間をおろそかにしていた。
examples.en: I was so wrapped up in work that I neglected time with my family.

examples.jp: 忙しさにかまけて、ずっと連絡していなかった。
examples.en: I was so caught up in being busy that I hadn't been in touch.

29.summary: にかまけて means being so absorbed in X that something else gets neglected.
29.details:
仕事**にかまけて**、家族との時間をおろそかにしていた。
*(I was so wrapped up in work that I neglected time with my family.)*
忙しさ**にかまけて**、ずっと連絡していなかった。
*(I was so caught up in being busy that I hadn't been in touch.)*

Often used as an apology or self-criticism. The second clause describes neglect (おろそかにする, 〜ていなかった). 忙しさにかまけて is a common excuse in letters.

29.title: 〜かたわら
29.structure: Verb (Dictionary) / Noun + の + かたわら
29.explanation: Doing a second activity alongside one's main occupation over a long period.

examples.jp: 彼は会社に勤めるかたわら、小説を書いている。
examples.en: He writes novels while working at a company.

examples.jp: 彼女は子育てのかたわら、大学で勉強を続けた。
examples.en: She continued studying at university alongside raising her children.

29.summary: かたわら describes a second, long-term activity alongside one's main work.
29.details:
彼は会社に勤める**かたわら**、小説を書いている。
*(He writes novels while working at a company.)*
彼女は子育ての**かたわら**、大学で勉強を続けた。
*(She continued studying at university alongside raising her children.)*

Unlike ながら (which is moment-to-moment), かたわら describes two roles over a long period. The first is usually the main job. かたわら alone also means 'beside' (道のかたわら).

29.title: 〜がてら
29.meaning: While (doing) ~ / On the way ~ / Taking the opportunity of ~
29.structure: Noun (する-noun) / Verb (ます-stem) + がてら
29.explanation: Doing one thing while also using the chance to do another, usually something involving going somewhere.

examples.jp: 散歩がてら、パンを買いに行った。
examples.en: I went to buy bread while out for a walk.

examples.jp: 駅まで送りがてら、少し話をした。
examples.en: We had a little talk while I walked them to the station.

29.summary: がてら means doing a second thing at the same time as the first — 'while out doing X'.
29.details:
散歩**がてら**、パンを買いに行った。
*(I went to buy bread while out for a walk.)*
駅まで送り**がてら**、少し話をした。
*(We had a little talk while I walked them to the station.)*

The second action is usually movement (行く, 来る, 歩く). Typical first actions: 散歩, 買い物, 見物. Unlike かたわら, がてら is short-term and casual.

29.title: 〜かたがた
29.explanation: A formal way of saying one action serves two purposes, typically in letters and business.

examples.jp: お礼かたがた、ご挨拶に伺いました。
examples.en: I came to greet you and also to thank you.

examples.jp: 近況報告かたがた、お手紙を差し上げます。
examples.en: I'm writing to you partly to let you know how I'm doing.

29.summary: かたがた is a formal 'while also' — one visit or letter serves two purposes.
29.details:
お礼**かたがた**、ご挨拶に伺いました。
*(I came to greet you and also to thank you.)*
近況報告**かたがた**、お手紙を差し上げます。
*(I'm writing to you partly to let you know how I'm doing.)*

Very formal; used in business letters and polite visits. Typical nouns: お礼, お詫び, ご挨拶, ご報告, お見舞い. The second clause is usually 伺う, 参る, or a letter.

30.title: 〜といい〜といい
30.meaning: Both ~ and ~ / In terms of ~ as well as ~
30.structure: Noun A + といい + Noun B + といい
30.explanation: Gives two examples to show that something is outstanding (or bad) in every respect.

examples.jp: 味といい値段といい、この店は文句なしだ。
examples.en: Both the taste and the price are perfect at this restaurant.

examples.jp: 顔といい性格といい、彼は父親にそっくりだ。
examples.en: In both looks and personality, he's just like his father.

30.summary: といい〜といい lists two aspects to show that something is X in every respect.
30.details:
味**といい**値段といい、この店は文句なしだ。
*(Both the taste and the price are perfect at this restaurant.)*
顔**といい**性格といい、彼は父親にそっくりだ。
*(In both looks and personality, he's just like his father.)*

Used to evaluate (praise, criticism, surprise), not for neutral listing. Compare にしても〜にしても and であれ〜であれ, which mean 'whether A or B'.

30.title: 〜なり〜なり
30.structure: Noun / Verb (Dictionary) + なり + Noun / Verb (Dictionary) + なり
30.explanation: Suggests choosing from examples — 'X or Y, whatever suits you'.

examples.jp: 分からなければ、先生に聞くなり辞書で調べるなりしなさい。
examples.en: If you don't understand, ask the teacher or look it up in a dictionary.

examples.jp: 電話なりメールなりで連絡してください。
examples.en: Please get in touch by phone or email or whatever.

30.summary: なり〜なり suggests a choice among examples — 'X or Y, whichever'.
30.details:
分からなければ、先生に聞く**なり**辞書で調べるなりしなさい。
*(If you don't understand, ask the teacher or look it up in a dictionary.)*
電話**なり**メールなりで連絡してください。
*(Please get in touch by phone or email or whatever.)*

Used for suggestions, advice and commands. It's not used for past events. 何なり means 'anything': 何なりとお申し付けください ('please ask for anything'). Different from なり ('as soon as', Lesson 4).

30.title: 〜だの〜だの
30.structure: Noun / Verb・Adj (Plain) + だの + ... + だの
30.explanation: Lists examples with a tone of complaint or irritation.

examples.jp: 彼は暑いだの疲れただのと、文句ばかり言っている。
examples.en: He's always complaining — it's too hot, he's tired, and so on.

examples.jp: 引っ越しの前は、掃除だの手続きだので忙しい。
examples.en: Before moving, I'm busy with cleaning, paperwork and whatnot.

30.summary: だの〜だの lists things with a complaining tone — 'this and that and so on'.
30.details:
彼は暑い**だの**疲れただのと、文句ばかり言っている。
*(He's always complaining — it's too hot, he's tired, and so on.)*
引っ越しの前は、掃除**だの**手続きだので忙しい。
*(Before moving, I'm busy with cleaning, paperwork and whatnot.)*

Conversational and usually negative. Often followed by と言う or と文句を言う. Compared with やら〜やら (N2), だの〜だの is more critical.

30.title: 〜かれ〜かれ
30.structure: い-Adj (stem) + かれ + opposite い-Adj (stem) + かれ
30.explanation: A classical pattern used in a few fixed pairs of opposites, meaning 'whether X or Y'.

examples.jp: 遅かれ早かれ、真実は明らかになるだろう。
examples.en: Sooner or later, the truth will come out.

examples.jp: 人は多かれ少なかれ、悩みを抱えている。
examples.en: Everyone has worries to a greater or lesser degree.

30.summary: かれ〜かれ means 'whether X or Y', in a few fixed pairs like 遅かれ早かれ.
30.details:
**遅かれ早かれ**、真実は明らかになるだろう。
*(Sooner or later, the truth will come out.)*
人は**多かれ少なかれ**、悩みを抱えている。
*(Everyone has worries to a greater or lesser degree.)*

Only in set phrases: 遅かれ早かれ ('sooner or later'), 多かれ少なかれ ('more or less'), 善かれ悪しかれ ('for better or worse'). It's not productive with other adjectives.

31.title: 〜つ〜つ
31.structure: Verb A (ます-stem) + つ + Verb B (ます-stem) + つ
31.explanation: Two opposite actions alternate back and forth, in set phrases.

examples.jp: 二人は抜きつ抜かれつのレースを続けた。
examples.en: The two kept overtaking each other throughout the race.

examples.jp: 持ちつ持たれつの関係が大切だ。
examples.en: A relationship of mutual support is important.

31.summary: つ〜つ describes two opposite actions alternating — in fixed phrases.
31.details:
二人は**抜きつ抜かれつ**のレースを続けた。
*(The two kept overtaking each other throughout the race.)*
**持ちつ持たれつ**の関係が大切だ。
*(A relationship of mutual support is important.)*

Fixed expressions only: 行きつ戻りつ ('back and forth'), 抜きつ抜かれつ ('neck and neck'), 持ちつ持たれつ ('give and take'), 差しつ差されつ ('pouring drinks for each other'). Often an active verb paired with its passive.

31.title: 〜ともなく／〜ともなしに
31.meaning: Without meaning to ~ / Idly ~ / (with question words) Some ~ or other
31.structure: Verb (Dictionary) + ともなく・ともなしに / Question word + (particle) + ともなく
31.explanation: Doing something without any clear intention; with question words, it means it's unclear who, where or when.

examples.jp: テレビを見るともなく見ていたら、友達が映っていた。
examples.en: I was idly watching TV when a friend of mine appeared on screen.

examples.jp: どこからともなく、いい匂いがしてきた。
examples.en: A nice smell drifted in from somewhere or other.

31.summary: ともなく means doing something absent-mindedly, or (with question words) 'from somewhere or other'.
31.details:
テレビを見る**ともなく**見ていたら、友達が映っていた。
*(I was idly watching TV when a friend of mine appeared on screen.)*
どこから**ともなく**、いい匂いがしてきた。
*(A nice smell drifted in from somewhere or other.)*

With verbs, the same verb often repeats: 見るともなく見る, 聞くともなく聞く. With question words: どこからともなく, 誰からともなく, いつからともなく. Literary.

31.title: 〜かいもなく
31.structure: Verb (た-form) / Noun + の + かいもなく
31.explanation: Efforts were made, but they didn't produce the hoped-for result.

examples.jp: 必死の看病のかいもなく、祖父は亡くなった。
examples.en: Despite our desperate nursing, my grandfather passed away.

examples.jp: 一生懸命勉強したかいもなく、試験に落ちてしまった。
examples.en: All my hard study was in vain — I failed the exam.

31.summary: かいもなく means 'efforts were in vain'.
31.details:
必死の看病の**かいもなく**、祖父は亡くなった。
*(Despite our desperate nursing, my grandfather passed away.)*
一生懸命勉強した**かいもなく**、試験に落ちてしまった。
*(All my hard study was in vain — I failed the exam.)*

かい (甲斐) means 'worth, effect'. The positive form is かいがある ('worth it'): 頑張ったかいがあった. Common with 努力, 看病, 応援.

31.title: 〜とは (Surprise)
31.explanation: Expresses surprise, shock or admiration at a fact, often leaving the rest of the sentence unsaid.

examples.jp: あの彼が会社の社長になるとは。
examples.en: To think that he of all people would become company president!

examples.jp: こんな所で昔の友達に会うとは思わなかった。
examples.en: I never thought I'd meet an old friend in a place like this.

31.summary: とは at the end of a clause expresses surprise — 'to think that...!'.
31.details:
あの彼が会社の社長になる**とは**。
*(To think that he of all people would become company president!)*
こんな所で昔の友達に会う**とは**思わなかった。
*(I never thought I'd meet an old friend in a place like this.)*

Often the sentence ends right after とは, or continues with 驚いた, 思わなかった, 信じられない. It's a stronger version of なんて. Different from the defining とは ('X means...').

32.title: 〜かと思いきや
32.structure: Sentence (Plain) + かと思いきや / 〜と思いきや
32.explanation: The speaker expected one thing, but the result was the opposite.

examples.jp: 簡単な試験かと思いきや、意外に難しかった。
examples.en: I thought it would be an easy exam, but it was surprisingly hard.

examples.jp: 雨がやんだと思いきや、また降り出した。
examples.en: Just when I thought the rain had stopped, it started again.

32.summary: かと思いきや means 'I thought X, but actually Y' — expectation overturned.
32.details:
簡単な試験**かと思いきや**、意外に難しかった。
*(I thought it would be an easy exam, but it was surprisingly hard.)*
雨がやんだ**と思いきや**、また降り出した。
*(Just when I thought the rain had stopped, it started again.)*

The second clause often has 意外にも, 実は, また. It's used in writing and somewhat playfully in speech. Compare かと思うと (N2), where the second event really happens right after.

32.title: 〜といったところだ
32.meaning: About ~ / At most ~ / More or less ~
32.structure: Noun / Verb (Plain) + といったところだ
32.explanation: Gives a rough estimate or evaluation, usually implying 'not much'.

examples.jp: 参加者は多くても20人といったところだ。
examples.en: There'll be about twenty participants at most.

examples.jp: 私の英語力は、日常会話ができるといったところです。
examples.en: My English is about good enough for everyday conversation.

32.summary: といったところだ gives a modest estimate — 'roughly X, at most'.
32.details:
参加者は多くても20人**といったところだ**。
*(There'll be about twenty participants at most.)*
私の英語力は、日常会話ができる**といったところです**。
*(My English is about good enough for everyday conversation.)*

Often with せいぜい or 多くても, showing the amount is small. It's also used to describe something as 'more or less' a certain level. というところだ is a variant.

32.title: 〜ところを
32.meaning: Although (you are) ~ / At the moment when ~
32.structure: Verb/い-Adj (Plain) / な-Adj + な / Noun + の + ところを
32.explanation: Mostly in polite set phrases: acknowledging someone's situation (busy, tired) when asking or thanking. Also 'at the moment when'.

examples.jp: お忙しいところを、わざわざありがとうございます。
examples.en: Thank you for taking the time when you're so busy.

examples.jp: 犯人は逃げようとしたところを捕まった。
examples.en: The criminal was caught just as he tried to run away.

32.summary: ところを acknowledges the listener's situation in polite phrases, or means 'at the moment when'.
32.details:
お忙しい**ところを**、わざわざありがとうございます。
*(Thank you for taking the time when you're so busy.)*
犯人は逃げようとした**ところを**捕まった。
*(The criminal was caught just as he tried to run away.)*

Polite set phrases: お忙しいところを, お休みのところを, お疲れのところを — followed by thanks or an apology. The 'at the moment' use comes with verbs of catching or seeing (捕まる, 見られる).

32.title: 〜ものとする
32.meaning: Shall be ~ / Is to be regarded as ~
32.explanation: A formal expression used in contracts and rules to set a condition or interpretation.

examples.jp: 期限までに返事がない場合は、欠席とみなすものとする。
examples.en: If no reply is received by the deadline, it shall be regarded as absence.

examples.jp: 本契約は、署名の日から有効になるものとする。
examples.en: This contract shall take effect from the date of signature.

32.summary: ものとする is legal and official 'shall be' language.
32.details:
期限までに返事がない場合は、欠席とみなす**ものとする**。
*(If no reply is received by the deadline, it shall be regarded as absence.)*
本契約は、署名の日から有効になる**ものとする**。
*(This contract shall take effect from the date of signature.)*

Found in contracts, regulations and terms of service. It sets an agreed interpretation, not a fact. 〜ものと思われる ('it is believed that') is another formal use of ものと.
